author: luca_zanolini
content:
<@755590043632140352> 

It seems possible to me for process_attestation to double-count equivocating attesters in payment.weight.

The credit fires whenever an inclusion sets a new participation flag (will_set_new_flag). Since TIMELY_SOURCE and TIMELY_TARGET are separate flags, a validator that equivocates on the target is credited twice right? 

A1 (right source, wrong target) sets TIMELY_SOURCE on the first inclusion; A2 (right source, right target) then sets TIMELY_TARGET (a new flag so credited again). Both point at the canonical slot-N block, so both are same-slot and hit the same payment entry.

This contradicts the "each validator contributes exactly once per slot" comment. The equivocation is slashable, but no attester-slashing path touches payment.weight, so the extra credit survives. 

Am I missing something or is this a concern?

author: potuz
content:
Hmmm, I'm still a little sleepy but this seems valid to me! the FFM-LMD check that would prevent these sort of slashings is only applied on `on_attestation` which happens when inserting on forkchoice, but not on block processing.  Worst part is that this is my doing, when looking at that function I wanted to avoid the per flag looping. Just checking if it's going to add the target flag should be enough.

I will leave this to theoreticians if they want to change the loop to deal with this. Here are some comments:

1. One of the equivocations **cannot gossip**, this is because one of the attestations is for certain not FFG-LMD compatible and gossip checks this path, so the only one that can include these attestations is the proposer. 
2. This can only change trustless payment weight by substantially slashing a set of validators, which have to be owned by the single proposer by the above point. So that block must have been worth a whole lot of money 😅 

Either we can do a single loop to check if any flag was set before, or we can just change that flag on right target (this adds a new if on that loop). The latter approach was the original design if I remember correctly, and then I changed it back to avoid extra checks. 

It's a simple change if people want to fix this though, and it's statically testable, so probably it's not a big deal to change this so late.
